svg.text: Two setters across from each other. The back-row setter sets; the front-row setter attacks.
Filled circle = the setter who sets in that rotation. Write your players’ numbers on the # lines.
• 6-2: the setter in the back row sets. The setter in the front row plays as a right-side attacker.
• Because the setter always comes from the back row, there are three front-row attackers in every rotation.
• Many teams put the libero in for the middle blocker (MB) when the middle rotates to the back row.
S = setter · OH = outside hitter · MB = middle blocker · OPP = opposite · L = libero
Players rotate clockwise after each side-out: zone 2 moves to zone 1 and serves. This chart shows base positions, not serve-receive formations.
Drag your own players through all six rotations in the free RallyBoard app. It also flags overlap faults.
Free printable from RallyBoard, a volleyball rotation and tactics board app. Scan the code for the app and more sheets.
